text: Without limits, SQL Server hands out CPU and memory in the order it's asked for, so one noisy workload can starve everything else with no warning. Resource Governor puts a ceiling on how much a given workload can consume.

A resource pool is the actual ceiling. A workload group sits inside a pool and inherits its limits. A classifier function runs at login and decides which group a session belongs to. Miss RECONFIGURE and none of it takes effect.

Cap a reporting service account's workload group at 30% CPU and 25% memory, and even its worst query cannot exceed that ceiling — the OLTP workload's share is protected by the classifier function routing that login elsewhere.

Resource Governor is available on an Azure VM and Managed Instance, but not on Azure SQL Database, which solves the same problem through its own service-tier limits. Next up: recognizing a real bottleneck versus a query-design problem.
